new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accessible phonological sketch reports a (preliminary) two-way lexical tone contrast, low level vs low fall (e.g. za 'go' vs za 'jungle', bisi 'seed' vs bisi 'mongoose'), and gives no statement on the position or existence of word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Author states tone shapes are affected by voice quality and consonant elision (glottal stop from IA h- elided leaving a low-fall tone); flags the tonal analysis as preliminary. Vowel length said to be non-distinctive.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level minimal pairs in citation form; sub-dialects by clan (Karwa, Muo, Daingnya, Melong, Mongla, Langbasa, Angya gosa) noted but tone data not localized to one.
new_statements.identity_note: Debnath 2008 describes Tanchangya as spoken in the CHT (Bangladesh), CADC Mizoram and South Tripura (India), with clan-based sub-dialects (Karwa, Muo, Daingnya, Melong, Mongla, Langbasa, Angya gosa); all fall under tang1330 (no Glottolog sub-dialect codes). The closest described sister language is Chakma (chak1266), for which Huziwara 2019 reports a pitch accent system; that must not be transferred to Tanchangya without a source.

Nothing at all on stress or accent placement.
